answer: Probably yes: a meteg seems to be printed on צ with its tsere (first letter of צאתנו). I'm not sure enough of the host letter to resolve this.
visible_evidence: The whole word צאתנו and the marks under it are visible. A kamatz shows under ת. Below the line of points there is a short vertical stroke standing on its own. It is not joined to any letter or vowel. It sits at about the left edge of צ, near where צ meets א, just left of and a little below the two dots under צ, which read as a tsere. More dots appear to the left of the stroke, roughly under א, and I can't say for sure what they are. Because of that, and because the stroke sits so close to the צ/א boundary, I can't be certain the meteg belongs to צ rather than א. Meteg present: medium-high certainty. Host צ with tsere: medium.
